title: Test source-level fingerprints and compound-query retrieval
description: Third durable-memory indexing experiment following TASK-257. Freeze a generic implementation that derives bounded source-level fingerprints from registered evidence, composes diverse evidence slots, and decomposes compound questions before any new truth set is authored. Run the known TASK-257 questions only as a labeled development regression, then use one fresh visible read-only helper to author a new older-corpus holdout including at least one valid no-match query and a different fresh visible helper to evaluate one compact packet at a time. Measure task/source precision and recall, no-match handling, context, latency, path health, and scope. Do not integrate into startup, routing, Command Center, or external services.
acceptance_criteria: The retrieval implementation is frozen before the independent author produces the new truth set, and the known TASK-257 questions are clearly labeled development regression rather than holdout evidence.

Every registered source receives a deterministic bounded content-derived fingerprint with evidence role, task linkage, path health, and no owner-authored semantic answer fields; packet evidence selection enforces role diversity.
Compound-query decomposition is deterministic and bounded, and the fresh holdout contains at least one legitimate no-match question with explicit abstention scoring.

A fresh visible read-only author and a different fresh visible read-only evaluator stay within compact-packet scopes; the final report compares regression and fresh-holdout task/source metrics, context, latency, path health, and limitations without making an integration claim.
